What I Work On

PhD Research Focus

My PhD at QUT's Centre for Microbiome Research investigates the functional significance of small proteins — an underexplored frontier in microbial genomics. I use gene synteny as a lens to decode what these tiny molecules do within their genomic and ecological context.

🧬

Gene Synteny Analysis

Leveraging conserved genomic neighbourhood patterns across microbial genomes to infer the function of unannotated small proteins — turning positional context into biological insight.

🔬

Small Protein Discovery

Identifying and characterising small open reading frames (sORFs) and the micropeptides they encode across gut metagenomes, with a focus on their roles in host-microbe interactions.

💻

Computational Metagenomics

Developing and applying bioinformatic pipelines — using Python, R, and Linux — for metagenomic data analysis, statistical modelling, and machine learning-driven candidate prioritisation.

Background

About Me

I'm a first-year PhD student at Queensland University of Technology's Centre for Microbiome Research, based in Brisbane, Australia. My doctoral work focuses on decoding the function of small proteins using gene synteny — combining computational genomics with microbiome science to understand what these undercharacterised molecules do.

I hold an MSc in Bioinformatics from Amity University and a BSc in Biotechnology from Osmania University. With experience spanning industry, clinical bioinformatics, and academic research across India and Australia, I bring a broad perspective to computational microbiome science.
